## Transport & background

| ID | Claim | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [`elsepa-vendor-reference`](ledger-transport-background.md#elsepa-vendor-reference) | the shipped ELSEPA 2020 free-atom deck writer and parser preserve the vendor's native energy/angular grids, differential and integrated elastic cross sections, and construct a monotone normalized angular CDF before any later energy interpolation | `filtered` |
| [`bremslib-library-reference`](ledger-transport-background.md#bremslib-library-reference) | the BremsLib v2.0.8 library reader preserves the vendor's native `(T1, k/T1)` and ragged angular grids, the `k/Z**2` scaling of both cross sections, and the finite- versus point-nucleus distinction, and reproduces the vendor's own published angular integral of each DDCS node, from which the normalized angular shape function follows with unit solid-angle integral | `filtered` |
| [`bremslib-angular-model`](ledger-transport-background.md#bremslib-angular-model) | `cross_section_model="bremslib"` weights each transport segment by the BremsLib v2.0 double differential cross section at its emission angle, `d2sigma/(dk dOmega) = (Z**2/k) chi(T, k/T) S(T, k/T, theta)` with `cos(theta) = v_hat . n_hat`, taking the photon-energy spectrum `dsigma/dk = (Z**2/k) chi` from the same evaluation; PyRITE's own interpolation keeps `integral(d2sigma/(dk dOmega) dOmega) = dsigma/dk` exactly at every `(T, k)` | `filtered` |
| [`electron-transport`](ledger-transport-background.md#electron-transport) | Joy–Luo slowing-down (**low-energy branch only** since `relativistic-bethe-stopping` landed) + Mott/screened-Rutherford elastic scattering → radiating segments | `rederived` |
| [`relativistic-bethe-stopping`](ledger-transport-background.md#relativistic-bethe-stopping) | Berger–Seltzer/ICRU-37 relativistic collision stopping, spliced onto Joy–Luo per element at each element's own crossover | `rederived` |
| [`energy-loss-straggling`](ledger-transport-background.md#energy-loss-straggling) | optional unrestricted Urban energy-loss fluctuations applied per element as a compound-Poisson sum of two excitation levels and a $1/\epsilon^2$ continuum up to the Moller ceiling $T_{\max}=E/2$. The analytic channel model uses the supplied spliced stopping magnitude $C=\lvert dE/dx\rvert$, so $\langle\Delta E\rangle=Cs$ exactly and $\operatorname{Var}(\Delta E)=s(\Sigma_1E_1^2+\Sigma_2E_2^2+\Sigma_3E_0T_{\max})$. Counts are exact Poisson at every supported mean: means above 64 are split into independent bounded-rate chunks whose counts sum by Poisson additivity. It is applied on every host core and exact CUDA; the default-off path is bit-for-bit historical | `rederived` |
| [`gpu-transport-core`](ledger-transport-background.md#gpu-transport-core) | run-to-completion per-electron transport (CPU core and its CUDA port) samples the SAME distribution as the lockstep core: identical models, identical draw semantics, one counter-addressed SplitMix64 stream per electron instead of one shared step-major stream. No new equation — a sampling-order claim over `electron-transport`. `transport_core="auto"` (the default) takes the CUDA core when the process has a CUDA device, the run is ungrooved, and `Ne > 1000` | `filtered` |
| [`transport-midpoint-stopping`](ledger-transport-background.md#transport-midpoint-stopping) | `energy_model="midpoint"` advances a physical flight by explicit midpoint RK2: `E_pred = E_start + (dE/ds)(E_start)·s`, then `E_end = E_start + (dE/ds)((E_start+E_pred)/2)·s`. The clock uses `Δt = s/β((E_start+E_end)/2)`. The cutoff branch separately defines `s_cut = (E_cut−E_start)/(dE/ds)((E_start+E_cut)/2)` and assigns `E_end = E_cut`; it is not an inversion of the explicit RK2 step. Replaces the left-endpoint (frozen) rule that held `dE/ds` and `β` at `E_start` over the whole flight. Elastic hazard stays frozen within each row; substeps re-evaluate it at the next row start | `discrepancy` |
| [`energy-controlled-propagation`](ledger-transport-background.md#energy-controlled-propagation) | `max_dE_frac=f` (which requires `energy_model="midpoint"`) splits a physical flight using the deterministic left-endpoint control `s_cap=f E_start/C(E_start)`. This bounds the predicted mean loss, not the realized midpoint or Urban loss. The elastic collision is drawn ONCE per physical flight as an optical depth `tau = -ln(U)` and consumed across the flight's substeps at each substep's own hazard, `tau -= ds/lambda(E_substep)`; the flight closes when the budget is exhausted, at a boundary, at the cutoff, or on termination. A cap-limited substep keeps the flight's direction, `flight_id`, and remaining `tau`, increments `substep_id`, and never scatters. Rows carry `electron_id`/`flight_id`/`substep_id`, so the stable physical key is `(electron_id, flight_id)` | `rederived` |
| [`substep-radiation-invariance`](ledger-transport-background.md#substep-radiation-invariance) | a numerical substep is integration detail, not an emitter, so refining `max_dE_frac` at fixed physical flights refines the quadrature of what each flight radiates and nothing else. Two rules. (1) The DEFAULT (incoherent) CXR reduction groups by physical flight: rows sharing `(electron_id, flight_id)` are summed as complex field and the sum is squared, `I = sum_flights \|sum_{substeps} A_k Q_k\|^2`, replacing per-row `sum_rows \|A_j Q_j\|^2`; only whole flights add incoherently. (2) Both radiation kernels evaluate a row at the propagator's representative energy `E_repr = (E_start + E_end)/2`, which midpoint transport now emits as `E_repr_keV`, making each row's one-point path integral a midpoint rather than a left-endpoint rule and making the line kernel's `t_L = L/beta(E_repr)` exactly the transported flight duration `t_end - t_start`. Frozen rows carry no `E_repr_keV` and every group is a singleton, so production output is bit-for-bit historical | `discrepancy` |
| [`radiation-error-estimators`](ledger-transport-background.md#radiation-error-estimators) | host-side, opt-in per-flight estimators of the error the radiation kernels make by evaluating emission coefficients at the flight's start energy: (1) CXR endpoint resonance drift — the sweep of `E_res = ħc·v·g/(1−v·n)` between the flight's endpoint speeds (each with its own Doppler denominator), in units of the flight's sinc half-width `W = 2πħc/(dnm·t_L)`; (2) bremsstrahlung endpoint quadrature error — the grid-integrated (trapezoid) relative difference between the kernel's left-endpoint `n·dsigma/dk(T_start)·L` and a midpoint evaluation, per flight. p50/p90/p99/max summaries; warning when p99 exceeds the calibrated threshold | `rederived` |
| [`energy-step-convergence`](ledger-transport-background.md#energy-step-convergence) | measured convergence of transport observables and radiation reductions under refinement of the numerical energy step, and selection of the step-control variable for slices F–H. (1) Transport: frozen vs midpoint propagation shifts no exit fraction, retained energy, or transit clock beyond 1.6σ at Ne=4000 over 14 cases; the one resolved shift is mean path length in C 5 keV thick, where the left-endpoint rule overstates the CSDA range by 1.2% because the Joy–Luo stopping magnitude grows as E falls. (2) The 2%/1% fractional-loss rungs are no-ops: the elastic mean free path already holds per-flight loss below 2% for ~99% of flights. (3) The binding constraint for coherent CXR is the ABSOLUTE emission phase dφ = (E_res/ħc)·dt, accumulated along a trajectory, not fractional energy loss; accepted tolerance p99 < 0.1 rad. The midpoint rule meets it at one row per flight (1e-3–6e-2 rad) while the frozen rule does not meet it at any rung (11–1300 rad, first order in f) | `rederived` |
| [`longitudinal-bunch-sampling`](ledger-transport-background.md#longitudinal-bunch-sampling) | centered legacy Gaussian/uniform/explicit offsets plus resolved Gaussian, compressed, and directly indexed wavelength-matched microtrain sampling, kept separate from transport age | `rederived` |
| [`beam-phase-space-metrics`](ledger-transport-background.md#beam-phase-space-metrics) | sampled RMS sizes, transverse/longitudinal covariance emittance, Twiss parameters, normalized emittance, Gaussian-equivalent peak current, and pulse average current | `rederived` |
| [`beam-phase-space-injection`](ledger-transport-background.md#beam-phase-space-injection) | Courant–Snyder transverse injection: stored normalized emittance, geometric `ε_g = ε_n/(βγ)` per case, per-plane Gaussian draw `x = sqrt(ε_gβ_T)·u₁`, `x' = sqrt(ε_g/β_T)·(u₂ − α u₁)` at the crystal entrance face | `rederived` |
